title: VocalGrad: Evaluating Acoustic Perception in Audio Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.23745v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Recent large audio language models (LALMs) have extended their capabilities beyond lexical speech understanding to tasks requiring paralinguistic and non-linguistic audio understanding, such as emotion recognition. However, these models still struggle to reliably utilize acoustic information, particularly when it co-occurs with spoken linguistic content. Existing benchmarks do not clearly distinguish acoustic perception from higher-level reasoning, making it difficult to identify the source of these failures. To address this issue, we introduce VocalGrad, a benchmark designed to evaluate LALMs' ability to perceive low-level acoustic variations. VocalGrad formulates this problem as a simple binary classification of temporal change direction, enabling evaluation largely independent of higher-level reasoning or semantic understanding. translated_title: VocalGrad：评估音频语言模型中的声学感知能力
translated_abstract: 近期的大规模音频语言模型（LALMs）已将其能力扩展到超越词汇层面的语音理解，能够处理需要副语言和非语言音频理解的任务，例如情感识别。然而，这些模型仍然难以可靠地利用声学信息，尤其是当声学信息与口头语言内容同时出现时。现有的基准测试未能清晰地区分声学感知与更高层次的推理，因此难以确定这些失败的根源。为了解决这一问题，我们提出了VocalGrad，一个旨在评估LALMs感知低级声学变化能力的基准测试。VocalGrad将这一问题表述为一个简单的时间变化方向二元分类任务，使得评估在很大程度上独立于更高层次的推理或语义理解。我们的基准测试结果显示，人类标注者与最先进的模型之间在声学感知能力上存在显著差距。
tldr: 本文提出VocalGrad基准，通过将低级声学变化感知转化为时间变化方向的二元分类任务来评估音频语言模型的声学感知能力，并揭示了模型与人类标注者之间的显著感知差距。
